chunks: And Ahmad ibn 'Abdun informed me, from Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Husayn ibn 'Abd al-Malik al-Awdi, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Ziyad al-Karkhi, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him):

who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: «Three [acts] — whoever commits them is accursed: one who defecates in the shade of the travelers' resting place, one who withholds shared water, and one who blocks a frequented road.»

key_terms.اَلنُّزَّالِ: travelers who descend/stop to encamp; their resting and shaded area
key_terms.اَلْمَسْلُوكِ: traveled, frequented — a road regularly traversed by people
key_terms.اَلْمُنْتَابَ: shared, frequented — water visited in turns by the community (from intaba: to visit repeatedly)
key_terms.مَلْعُونٌ: accursed, one upon whom divine curse (la'na) falls

ai.seo_question: What three acts did the Prophet (SAWW) declare as accursed in this hadith from Tahdhib al-Ahkam, chapter on etiquette of acts necessitating tahara?
ai.summary: Transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) from the Prophet (SAWW), this hadith declares three acts as accursed (mal'un): relieving oneself in the shaded rest area of traveling wayfarers (al-nuzzal), withholding communally shared water, and obstructing a frequented road. Situated in a chapter on the etiquette of acts necessitating tahara, the hadith frames public hygiene and communal rights within the prophetic ethical and legal tradition.
